text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 2440 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS

- Prime Minister Gyula Horn and Slovak Premier Vladimir Meciar held a round of bilateral talks in Postyen, Slovakia during Monday's second ever meeting between the heads of government of Hungary, Austria and Slovakia. @

- The head of the health insurance authority said that the situation has become chaotic after the State Audit Office and the Finance Ministry insisted that a decision on selecting a banking consortium to collect outstanding debts be postponed.

- The issue of politicians' links to privatisation surfaced again in Parliament yesterday when Young Democrat Mihaly Varga asked why a consortium with Socialist Party ties has paid only 100 million forints of the 600 million forint sale price of the machine factory Diosgyori Gepgyar. Finance Ministry State Secretary Laszlo Akar said the transaction will be examined.
- Opposition MPs presented an amendment of the Penal Code. @
- The agricultural cabinet has authorised the export of corn and flour following a dramatic drop in prices.
- The state privatisation and property management organisations received total revenues of 1,008 billion forints from privatisation between August 1990 and August 1996.
- Police will continue their campaign of nightclub raids until they find the person or persons behind last week's explosions and the murder of an underworld figure.
- Police have caught nine men and are searching for four others who held up train passsengers at knife point on the Dacia express between Bucharest and Vienna. @
VILAGGAZDASAG
- The executive presidential board of the Socialist Party parliamentary group has decided to make public its own assets statement on November 30 and recommends that party MPs do the same.
NEPSZABADSAG
- Free Democrat MP Tamas Bauer annexed a proposal for amendment to the conflict of interest bill, proposing to include MPs links to the private sector.
- Public employee wages will go up an average of 22 percent from February 1. @
- Tourism revenues are expected to total $2.3 billion this year, 30 percent more than in 1995.
MAGYAR HIRLAP

- A senior Foreign Ministry official Monday exuded optimism over the fact that political forces which support the Romanian-Hungarian basic treaty took leading positions in Sunday's Romanian parliamentary elections.

- Producer prices of pharmaceuticals will go up 9-11 percent from January according to an agreement between manufacturers and the Health Insurance Fund, said Richter Rt's Managing Director Erik Bogsch. @
- The Dutch bank ABN Amro has the best chance of purchasing the 94 percent stake in Magyar Hitel Bank. The winning bid will be selected today.

- The clothing company Styl Ruhagyar posted an after-tax profit of 165 million forints and a pre-tax profit of 212 million forints in the first nine months, down from 180 million and 254 million in October 1995.
MAGYAR NEMZET
- In Belgium, Defence Minister Gyorgy Keleti conferred with Belgian Defence Minister Jean-Pol Poncelet who said Belgium would willingly sell some F-16 fighter jets. @
- Interior Minister Gabor Kuncze will visit Moscow November 11-13 to discuss cooperation on combatting organised crime and drug trafficking.
